introduction: French has NO School-Based Assessment (SBA). Instead, the CSEC French examination carries a THIRD paper assessed orally: Paper 03, the Oral Examination, worth about 25-30% of the final grade. This guide prepares you for it. Paper 03 has three parts: (1) reading aloud a short passage in French; (2) five spoken responses to written situations, similar to the directed situations of Paper 02 but spoken; and (3) a guided conversation of about sixteen questions on your own life, your family, school, leisure, holidays and plans. Everything except the reading passage is spoken in French, and your examiner is trained to put you at ease. Practise aloud, every day, for short periods: pronunciation, fluency and the confidence to keep speaking when you make a mistake are what earn marks.

tasks.title: Reading a passage aloud in French
tasks.explanation: You are given a short passage (about 100-130 words) and a few minutes to read it silently. You then read it aloud. Marks are given for pronunciation (especially nasal vowels such as 'on', 'an', 'in'; the French 'r'; and final consonants, which are usually silent), for rhythm and phrasing at punctuation, and for audibility and pace. Practise by recording yourself, then reading along with a native recording of the same passage and imitating it. Read at a steady pace rather than speeding up; a slow, clear reading scores better than a rushed, unclear one.

tasks.title: Five spoken responses to given situations
tasks.explanation: You are given five short written situations (for example: 'You meet your teacher and greet her', 'You want to know the price of a kilo of rice') and you respond aloud in French, usually one sentence each. This is the spoken version of Section 1 of Paper 02, so the same preparation works for both. Decide 'tu' or 'vous' before you speak, and always complete the sentence; a fragment scores nothing.
tasks.marks: Five responses, each marked for the task achieved and the language used.

tasks.title: A conversation of about sixteen questions
tasks.explanation: The examiner asks you about yourself: your name, age, family, home, school, subjects, free time, sports, food, holidays, last weekend and your future plans. You are not expected to speak for a long time on each question, but you ARE expected to answer, and to add one detail or opinion rather than saying only 'oui' or 'non'. Prepare short, true answers about your own life and adapt them: the same sentences about your family, your school and your weekend answer most of the questions. If you do not understand, say 'Pardon, pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?' - that does not lose marks, but silence does.
tasks.marks: Marked for comprehension, range and accuracy across the conversation.

sampleTitle: Sample Paper 03 preparation - a prepared conversation

sample.body:
Passage: "Bonjour, je m'appelle Marc et j'habite à Castries, en Sainte-Lucie. Chaque matin, je me lève à six heures et je prends mon petit déjeuner avec ma famille. Je vais au lycée en bus ; le trajet dure vingt minutes. J'aime la biologie et le français, mais je n'aime pas les mathématiques. Le samedi, je joue au cricket avec mes amis et le dimanche je me repose."

Read it aloud three times: first for accuracy, then for rhythm, then in front of someone who will tell you whether you can be heard.
tips: Say the nasal vowels in 'bonjour' (on), 'matin' (in) and 'français' (an) in the throat, not with the English n.
Do not pronounce the final consonants of 'petit', 'déjeuner' and 'dix heures'.
Pause at every comma and full stop - phrasing is marked.

sample.body:
1. Greet your French teacher in the morning. -> "Bonjour, Madame. Comment allez-vous ?"
2. Ask a friend his age. -> "Quel âge as-tu ?"
3. Ask the price of a loaf of bread. -> "C'est combien le pain, s'il vous plaît ?"
4. Say what you did last weekend. -> "Le week-end dernier, je suis allé(e) à la plage avec ma famille."
5. Say what you want to do after your exams. -> "Après mes examens, je voudrais étudier l'informatique à l'université."
tips: Say the sentence out loud the moment you have thought of it; hesitation is not penalised, silence is.
Keep 'tu' for friends and 'vous' for adults - examiners notice.

sample.body:
Parle-moi de ta famille. -> "Nous sommes cinq à la maison : mon père, ma mère, mes deux sœurs et moi. Ma sœur aînée travaille dans un hôtel."

Quelles sont tes matières préférées ? -> "J'aime la biologie parce que c'est intéressant, mais je préfère le français parce que j'aime lire."

Qu'est-ce que tu fais le week-end ? -> "Le samedi, je joue au football avec mes amis et je fais de la natation ; le dimanche, je vais à l'église avec ma famille."

Quels sont tes projets ? -> "L'année prochaine, j'irai à l'université. Si j'obtiens une bourse, je voyagerai en France pour améliorer mon français."
tips: Add one extra detail to every answer: a reason, a time or an opinion.
Use the question's words in your answer - 'Quelles sont tes matières préférées ?' is answered with 'Mes matières préférées sont ...'.
Prepare four flexible answers (family, school, weekend, plans) and you can answer sixteen questions with them.

marking: Paper 03 is marked by your examiner against the CXC oral criteria: comprehension of the questions asked, fluency (the ability to keep speaking without long pauses), pronunciation and intonation, range of vocabulary and structures, and grammatical accuracy. Across the whole paper the Oral Examination is worth about 25-30% of the final CSEC French grade - more than any single written section except the composition - so it is worth preparing as seriously as Paper 02.
checklist: Record yourself reading a French passage aloud once a week and listen for the nasal vowels (on, an, in) and the silent final consonants.
Prepare and rehearse four flexible answers: my family, my school life, my weekend, my future plans.
Prepare one opinion sentence with a reason: "J'aime ... parce que ...".
Prepare one past sentence and one future sentence, so that every question can be answered in the tense it asks for.
Practise the situation responses of Paper 02 Section 1 aloud - they are the same task.
Learn the rescue phrases: "Pardon, pouvez-vous répéter ?", "Je ne comprends pas, s'il vous plaît.", "Un moment, s'il vous plaît."
Speak French for five minutes every day, out loud, even alone: fluency comes from practice, not from reading.
Remember: silence loses marks, a mistake does not. Keep talking, in French.
